title: UAE scientists harness AI to discover potential blood cancer drug
key_facts: Insilico Medicine, a clinical-stage biotech with scientists in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, says its researchers used AI to discover PROTACs, double-ended molecules that send a target protein to the cell's disposal system rather than just binding it.
The molecules target Bruton's tyrosine kinase, a protein that helps malignant cells grow in some leukaemias and lymphomas; details are published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
Insilico calls them 'lead compounds' because tests to qualify them for clinical trials are not complete.

Insilico says its AI platforms (PandaOmics for target discovery, Chemistry42 for molecule design) cut the time to select a drug candidate to 12 to 18 months versus two and a half to four years traditionally.
Nine of ten drugs that reach human testing fail to become approved medicines; organic chemist Ahmad Alghaith told The National AI's hope is to raise success rates and cut time and cost.
Earlier 2026 Insilico Abu Dhabi announcements: a potential brain cancer drug (April) and a non-opioid chronic pain candidate (July); human testing may take several years.
The Abu Dhabi Investment Office supported Insilico's UAE operations.
quote_evidence: Insilico Medicine describes the new PROTACs as “lead compounds”, because tests to determine whether they can enter clinical trials have not been completed.
“The hope of AI is that it will increase the success rate, reduce time spent and reduce costs,” he told The National.
Details have been published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI-designed class of protein-destroying molecules against blood cancer is at the early lead-compound stage, years from any patient.
notes: Company-sourced claims (timelines, success rates) reported by one outlet via interview; journal publication date not given.
